name: Hypoparathyroidism

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: European Society of Endocrinology Clinical Guidelines for Chronic Hypoparathyroidism

criteria.description: Low serum calcium (albumin-corrected total calcium or ionized calcium below normal range)
Inappropriately low or undetectable serum PTH level
Low urinary calcium excretion (in untreated state)
History of neck surgery (most common etiology) or known genetic/autoimmune cause

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Hypocalcemia with inappropriately low or absent PTH on at least two occasions, separated by at least 2 weeks, after exclusion of magnesium deficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Most common cause is post-surgical (after thyroidectomy or parathyroidectomy; ~75% of cases). Autoimmune, genetic (DiGeorge, HDR syndrome, autosomal dominant hypocalcemia), and idiopathic causes make up the remainder.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chvostek sign (facial muscle twitching on tapping facial nerve)
pathognomonic.notes: Sensitivity ~70%; also positive in ~10% of normocalcemic individuals

pathognomonic.symptomName: Trousseau sign (carpal spasm with blood pressure cuff inflation)
pathognomonic.notes: More specific than Chvostek sign; inflate cuff 20 mmHg above systolic for 3 minutes

common.notes: Fingers, toes, and circumoral region most affected
Flexion of wrist and MCP joints with adduction of thumb

occasional.notes: Due to severe hypocalcemia; may be presenting feature
Life-threatening; due to tetany of laryngeal muscles

occasional.symptomName: Dry skin, coarse hair, brittle nails

rare.notes: Can cause extrapyramidal movement disorders; often incidental on imaging
Due to chronic hypocalcemia; may be bilateral
Complication of overtreatment with calcium and vitamin D

laboratory: Low urinary calcium in untreated state; elevated with treatment
Normal magnesium (must exclude hypomagnesemia as cause)
imaging: CT head may show basal ganglia calcifications (Fahr syndrome pattern)
Renal ultrasound for nephrocalcinosis or renal stones (treatment complication)
DEXA scan may show increased bone density (reduced bone resorption from low PTH)
genetic: CaSR gain-of-function mutations (autosomal dominant hypocalcemia types 1 and 2)
GATA3 mutations (HDR syndrome: hypoparathyroidism, deafness, renal anomalies)
AIRE mutations (autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1 / APS-1)
GCM2 mutations (isolated autosomal recessive or dominant hypoparathyroidism)
other: ECG: prolonged QTc interval due to hypocalcemia
Chvostek and Trousseau signs on physical examination
Hearing assessment if HDR syndrome suspected
Assessment for other autoimmune endocrinopathies if autoimmune etiology

distinguishingFeatures: Albright hereditary osteodystrophy phenotype in PHP type 1a
Vitamin D deficiency has elevated PTH (secondary hyperparathyroidism)
Hypomagnesemia impairs PTH secretion and action
Calcium normalizes only after magnesium repletion
Characterized by rapid influx of calcium into bone
PTH may be low-normal but appropriate for the context

redFlags: Severe symptomatic hypocalcemia with tetany, seizures, or laryngospasm (medical emergency)
Prolonged QTc interval on ECG (risk of arrhythmia)
Nephrocalcinosis or declining renal function from overtreatment
DiGeorge syndrome phenotype in neonates (cardiac defects, immune deficiency, facial dysmorphism)
references: Bollerslev J, et al. European Society of Endocrinology Clinical Guideline: Treatment of chronic hypoparathyroidism in adults. Eur J Endocrinol. 2015;173(2):G1-20.
Shoback DM, et al. Presentation of Hypoparathyroidism: Etiologies and Clinical Features. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2016;101(6):2300-12.
Brandi ML, et al. Management of Hypoparathyroidism: Summary Statement and Guidelines. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2016;101(6):2273-83.
Clarke BL, et al. Epidemiology and Diagnosis of Hypoparathyroidism. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2016;101(6):2284-99.
